requirements.evidence: Contract is implemented: routes/web.php:18-42 defines login/register/logout/home, password.* and verification.* with the required methods and middleware; Login/Register expose the required public properties and submit() (app/Livewire/Auth/Login.php:16-22, app/Livewire/Auth/Register.php:18-21); Password::defaults() is set once (app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:25); User implements MustVerifyEmail (app/Models/User.php:14); .env.example:1,7 and phpunit.xml:22-23 pin pt_BR/en. Gaps: PasswordResetController redirects to login with a status flash (app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php:75) but the login view never renders session('status'); requirement 9 extends the route() rule to the pre-existing views but no change to welcome.blade.php/bulma-test.blade.php is in the diff.

conventions.evidence: Livewire validation mostly follows the pattern: Login uses #[Validate] (Login.php:16,19) and calls $this->validate() (Login.php:35). Register instead uses a rules() method (Register.php:73-79) with unannotated public properties (Register.php:18-21), inconsistent with the project pattern and its sibling. PasswordResetController validates three fields inline (PasswordResetController.php:53-57) although the convention asks for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two. Docs/CHANGELOG are updated (CHANGELOG.md:12-13, docs/business-rules.md:68-76) and the Blade component/layout conventions are followed (resources/views/components/form-field.blade.php:1-17).

security.evidence: No exploitable weakness found: failed logins and registrations are rate-limited (Login.php:39-43, Register.php:39-44), the login key lowercases email+IP (Login.php:67-70), verification is signed and compares the id and sha1 hash with hash_equals before marking verified (EmailVerificationController.php:31-39), reset rotates remember_token via forceFill (PasswordResetController.php:62-65), plain forms carry @csrf, all output uses {{ }}, and Livewire actions re-check Auth::check() (Login.php:29-33, Register.php:31-35).

tests.evidence: Extensive Pest suite: tests/Feature/Auth/LoginTest.php:12,73,102 cover locale, failed credentials and the five-attempt lockout; RegisterTest.php:53,95 cover confirmation and the per-IP limit; EmailVerificationTest.php:47 covers tampered-id 403; LogoutTest.php:8 covers session/token rotation; ForgotPasswordTest.php:43 and ResetPasswordTest.php:66 cover throttling and invalid tokens; LocalizationTest.php:5, PasswordRuleTest.php:6 and ViewConventionsTest.php:17 cover the cross-cutting requirements. Minor gap: no test asserts the reset status flash is visible on the login page.

simplicity.evidence: Reuses Laravel's password broker, ResetPassword/VerifyEmail notifications, named routes and middleware; one shared layout and one form-field component (resources/views/components/form-field.blade.php) avoid duplication. Minor: EmailVerificationController.php:31-39 manually reimplements the id/hash check that Laravel's EmailVerificationRequest already performs.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods with useful docblocks (EmailVerificationController.php:25-30, PasswordResetController.php:24-28, Login.php:24-26), clear names, no dead code or debug output; style and formatting match the surrounding Laravel/Livewire code.

scope.evidence: Only the auth task: Livewire components, controllers, routes, layout/views, lang files, locale config, tests, and the two docs updates (CHANGELOG.md:12-13, docs/business-rules.md:68-76); no entities/tenancy, mail theme, nginx/Docker, SCSS/JS or unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: PasswordResetController flashes a status and redirects to login (PasswordResetController.php:75), but the login view renders no session('status') block, so a user who just reset the password gets no confirmation.

Requirement 9 applies the route()/no-hardcoded-path rule to the pre-existing views, yet the diff changes neither, so compliance cannot be confirmed from the change (the added ViewConventionsTest at tests/Feature/ViewConventionsTest.php:17 will fail if either still hardcodes a path).

Register validates through a rules() method with unannotated public properties, while the project pattern and the sibling Login use #[Validate] attributes; rules() is allowed by the Livewire policy but is an unnecessary inconsistency here.
The reset endpoint validates three fields inline; the conventions call for a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.
The layout prints @livewireScripts but never @livewireStyles, so Livewire's loading-state styles are missing on every page.
The id/hash-403 logic duplicates what Laravel's EmailVerificationRequest already does; reusing the framework request would remove the manual check.

The rate-limit tests recompute RateLimiter::availableIn() and compare the exact auth.throttle message, which is time-sensitive and can flake at a second boundary; asserting the error key and message pattern would be sturdier.

The docs say password-reset "Forms are throttled to 6 requests per minute", but only password.email (and the verification endpoints) carries throttle:6,1; the reset POST is unthrottled, so the doc overstates the behavior.

review.summary: The change builds the complete session-auth flow (login/register/logout/home, password reset, signed e-mail verification) with Livewire/Bulma, pt-BR-first translations and a broad Pest suite, and the security mechanics (hashing, rate limits, hash_equals, CSRF, escaping) are sound. I would approve with nits: the reset status flash is never displayed on login, the pre-existing views are not shown to be route()-compliant, and a few conventions (Register's rules() vs #[Validate], inline validation at Form Request scale) slip.
